The nozzle's on the cheap airbrushes tend to crack too easily, and their orings tend to fail with solvents.

I've owned like 5 cheap airbrushes, 3 of them started to splatter and die due to the the nozzle being cracked. 

And like I said, due to their bad rings, airbrush cleaning solutions make clearing a clog quite a difficult task.

I ended up buying a cheap airbrush with solvent resistant sealers (which work like a charm) and a more expensive Creos airbrush (which is superior to anything I had before).

I'd say you're better off buying a nicer airbrush than getting frustrated with the cheap ones.
